newsitem.title: UK: Army base near Dunblane cemetery to stay closed.
newsitem.headline: Army base near Dunblane cemetery to stay closed.

text.p: An army firing range that lies in earshot of the cemetery where 13 children killed in the Dunblane massacre are buried is to be permanently shut down, Britain's defence ministry said on Wednesday.
Whitestone Range was temporarily closed in May because the sound of gunshots distressed bereaved families visiting the graves, the ministry said in a statement.
"The Army has concluded that to have re-opened it against the wishes of the bereaved families would have been inappropriate in the circumstances of this tragedy," it said.

Sixteen five- and six-year-olds and their teacher were shot dead in Dunblane school gymnasium in March by crazed weapons enthusiast Thomas Hamilton. Hamilton then killed himself with one of his four semi-automatic pistols.
The announcement that the range would be closed coincided with the publication of a report into the massacre by senior Judge Lord Cullen.
In response to the report, the government announced that it will ban the private ownership of most handguns.
